A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same HiLoFi, LoLoFi and LRKF research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on predictive uncertainty, MNIST classification and bandits, Kuairec recommendation, and Bayesian optimization, including appendix analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds sampling-strategy comparisons, CIFAR-10 evaluations and DrawNN rank experiments.

M1.justification: The stated predictive mean changes from Jacobian-times-parameters in v1 Equation (4) to the neural-network output in v2 Equation (10). This corrects the documented prediction formula; implementation changes are not established. The filtering updates and covariance structures remain essentially unchanged, and predictive sampling already appears in v1 Section 3.1.

E1.justification: V2 Appendix G.2 adds CIFAR-10 online classification, extending coverage from handwritten digits to natural color images. Existing MNIST, Kuairec, Bayesian-optimization and uncertainty tasks remain; moving MNIST classification into the appendix does not remove coverage.

E2.justification: The MNIST comparison adds explicit parameter-space Thompson-sampling variants of LoFi and LLL alongside predictive sampling (v2 Figure 2 and Table 2). V1's predictive-sampling curves labeled TS are matched to pBayes, not treated as new methods. Muon-epsilon leaves the main comparison but remains in the appendix; AdamW also participates in the added CIFAR-10 comparison.

E3.justification: V2 adds a 10,000-observation CIFAR-10 protocol using 1.7M- and 4.7M-parameter networks at ranks 1, 5 and 10, plus DrawNN rank sweeps. MNIST evaluation explicitly separates classical TS from predictive sampling, and appendix displays switch from relative reward to cumulative regret. These extend the evaluation while largely retaining existing benchmark settings.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix G.4.1 adds DrawNN-200 sensitivity experiments examining how HiLoFi and LRKF rank affects optimization performance and runtime. The CIFAR-10 experiment also compares ranks across two network capacities. Existing MNIST rank studies, covariance-error analysis and in-between uncertainty analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The MNIST tradeoff analysis changes its stated error bars from two standard deviations in v1 Appendix G.1.3 to one standard deviation in v2. New DrawNN rank figures explicitly report medians and interquartile ranges over 20 runs. No increase in repetitions for retained experiments is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantive results supporting sampling-efficiency and scalability claims. Table 2 reports LLL rewards of 13,922.3 for predictive sampling versus 7,201.9 for classical TS, with runtimes of 1.36 versus 191.55 minutes. Tables 4–5 and Figures 13–14 add CIFAR-10 and DrawNN rank results. The original Kuairec and Bayesian-optimization benchmark plots remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Proposition F.4 and its proof bound the one-step parameter-estimate difference between full-rank filtering and LRKF for a scalar linear model without parameter dynamics. Existing covariance-error bounds are retained. V2 also corrects the predictive-mean derivation in Corollary B.4 and a sign in the surrogate-covariance expression.

C1.justification: The central contribution of efficient, replay-free filtering with uncertainty-aware decisions remains. V2 adds explicit headline claims of 10–100 times faster inference than classical TS and scalability to million-parameter networks. Its title and abstract foreground the martingale-inspired perspective already discussed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 explains sampling speed through the lower dimensionality of outcome space and adds a one-step missing-data interpretation of the martingale framework in Section 3.3. It interprets the new rank and CIFAR-10 results as supporting efficiency and broader applicability. Existing limitations concerning smoothing, linearization, outliers and hyperparameters largely remain.

D1.justification: V2 supplies architecture, parameter-count, stream-size and rank details for the added CIFAR-10 experiment and changes the reported code-repository location. Existing hardware and most benchmark hyperparameter disclosures are retained. Both versions already provide code-access information; external availability was not verified.

R1.justification: V2 expands the existing martingale connection through Holmes and Walker and adds references supporting criticism of conventional Bayesian neural-network uncertainty, including Wenzel et al. Several earlier Bayesian and degenerate-Gaussian references are removed. Positioning shifts toward predictive sampling versus classical TS, while the core filtering-related literature remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, problem formulation and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten around predictive beliefs and sampling. V2 adds a martingale-background subsection, moves classification and optimizer discussion into the appendix, reorders proofs and algorithms, and adds an appendix contents page and checklist.

P2.justification: V2 adds strategy-comparison, performance, architecture and rank-result tables, converts notation prose into a table, and adds predictive-sampling pseudocode. MNIST plots are redesigned with separate sampling labels and regret axes; new DrawNN rank plots are added and the classification figure moves to the appendix. Many other graphics are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 clarifies predictive versus parameter sampling and strengthens support through direct comparisons, a restricted LRKF error bound, and scalability and rank studies. Reporting problems limit the gains: Table 4 describes accuracy but says lower is better, DrawNN timings disagree across presentations, and some MNIST captions mismatch their axes. The net improvement is useful but limited.
